mainTopic: Who is called to the Torah; reading from a חומש or a הפטרות scroll; writing a partial Torah scroll; whether the Torah was given scroll by scroll or complete.
overview: This amud first finishes a question about who is called to the Torah after the כהן, לוי, and ישראל. רבי יצחק נפחא gives a ranked list that starts with תלמידי חכמים who lead the community. Next comes a question: may the public reading be done from a חומש, a scroll with only one book? A proof from a ספר תורה missing one sheet is rejected, but רבה and רב יוסף still forbid it because of כבוד צבור. They also forbid reading from a scroll of only הפטרות. The גמרא rejects that ban and allows such a scroll, using the rule of עת לעשות לה׳, the same rule that allowed writing down אגדה. אביי then asks whether one may write a single Torah section for a child. רבה says no, and the גמרא defends this against challenges from הילני המלכה's golden tablet. Finally the גמרא shows the question is a dispute of תנאים. It brings רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש, who disagree whether the Torah was given scroll by scroll or all at once. It ends by starting רבי לוי's list of eight sections said on the day the משכן was set up, and that list continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Who is called up next, and no answer is ready
steps.stepSummary: The question asked just before this point ends here: after the כהן, לוי, and ישראל, who reads next? The scholar who was asked does not know.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who reads next? He did not have the answer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a question that began just before this point. The person who was asked had no answer, which sets up a trip to another רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gave the order כהן, then לוי, then ישראל. The question is how to rank everyone else after that. Because nobody has an answer yet, the next step will bring one from רבי יצחק נפחא.

keyTerms.meaning: they read, meaning who is called up to read from the Torah
literally 'it was not in his hand,' meaning he did not know the answer

phrases.english: who reads?
phrases.notes: This finishes the question just before it: after the כהן, לוי and ישראל of the משנה, who is called up next?

phrases.english: It was not in his hand.
phrases.notes: He means he had no answer ready.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי קוֹרְאִין? לָא הֲוָה בִּידֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a question that started just before this point.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: After כהן, לוי, and ישראל, in what order are the other people called to the Torah?

steps.title: רבי יצחק נפחא gives the ranked order
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק נפחא ranks who reads next: first תלמידי חכמים who are appointed leaders, then תלמידי חכמים fit to be leaders, then sons of תלמידי חכמים whose fathers were leaders, then heads of shuls, then anyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: He went and asked רבי יצחק נפחא, who told him: After them read Torah scholars who are appointed as leaders of the community. After them, Torah scholars who are fit to be appointed leaders. After them, sons of Torah scholars whose fathers are appointed leaders. After them, heads of synagogues, and then any person.
steps.whatsHappening: The question is taken to רבי יצחק נפחא, and he answers with a clear ranking of who is called up next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ranking is based on Torah learning together with service to the community. A scholar who actually serves as a leader comes first. A scholar who is qualified but not appointed comes next. After that come the sons of such leaders, then the heads of shuls, and finally everyone else.

keyTerms.meaning: Torah scholars
appointed leaders or managers of the community
those who are fit to be appointed
heads of the synagogues

steps.whatToRemember: After כהן, לוי, and ישראל, the order is: scholar-leaders, then scholars fit to lead, then sons of scholar-leaders, then heads of shuls, then anyone.

phrases.english: He came and asked Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha;
he said to him:
After them read Torah scholars
who are appointed as leaders over the community;
and after them, Torah scholars
who are fit to be appointed leaders over the community;
and after them, sons of Torah scholars
whose fathers are appointed leaders over the community;
and after them, heads of synagogues, and any person.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲתָא וְשַׁיְילֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יִצְחָק נַפָּחָא, אָמַר לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A ranked order: scholar-leaders, then scholars fit to lead, then sons of scholar-leaders, then heads of shuls, then anyone.

steps.title: May one read in shul from a single-book scroll?
steps.stepSummary: The people of the גליל ask רבי חלבו whether a public reading may be done from a חומש scroll. Neither he nor רבי יצחק נפחא knows, so the question goes to the בית מדרש.
steps.simpleTranslation: The people of the גליל sent a question to רבי חלבו: What is the law about reading from single-book scrolls in the synagogue in public? He did not know. He went and asked רבי יצחק נפחא, who did not know either. He went and asked in the study hall.
steps.whatsHappening: A new question opens: may the public reading be done from a scroll that has only one of the five books? Nobody knows, so the question is brought to the whole בית מדרש, which sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The issue is whether a public reading needs a complete ספר תורה, or whether a scroll holding one whole book is good enough. Two great רבנים do not know the answer, which shows this was a real open question.

keyTerms.meaning: scrolls that each contain only one of the five books of the Torah
in public, for the community's reading
the study hall

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלַחוּ לֵיהּ בְּנֵי גָלִיל לְרַבִּי חֶלְבּוֹ:
phrases.english: The people of the Galilee sent to Rabbi Chelbo:
What is the law about reading from single-book scrolls
phrases.notes: A חומש here is a scroll with only one of the five books, like a scroll of just בראשית.

phrases.english: in the synagogue, in public?
He did not have the answer.
He came and asked Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha;
he did not have the answer either.
He came and asked in the study hall,

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלַחוּ לֵיהּ בְּנֵי גָלִיל לְרַבִּי חֶלְבּוֹ: מַהוּ לִקְרוֹת בְּחוּמָּשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic that is still about the public Torah reading.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: May a public Torah reading be done from a scroll that contains only one book?

steps.title: Proof from a ספר תורה missing one sheet
steps.stepSummary: The בית מדרש answers from רבי יוחנן's rule that a ספר תורה missing even one sheet may not be read from. They conclude that a חומש, which is also not a complete Torah, may not be used either.
steps.simpleTranslation: They resolved it from what רבי שמואל בר נחמני said in the name of רבי יוחנן: A Torah scroll missing one sheet of parchment may not be read from.
steps.whatsHappening: The בית מדרש tries to settle the question with a proof from an existing rule of רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reasoning goes like this: if a ספר תורה missing just one sheet is already unfit for the public reading, then a scroll holding only one of the five books, which lacks much more, should surely be unfit too.

keyTerms.meaning: and they resolved it
one sheet of parchment in a Torah scroll
missing, lacking

phrases.english: and they resolved it from this
that Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said
that Rabbi Yochanan said:
A Torah scroll that is missing one sheet,
one does not read from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּפַשְׁטוּהָ מֵהָא דְּאָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 3 with a proof.
steps.raayaObject: That one may not read in public from a חומש scroll.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's rule that a ספר תורה missing one sheet may not be read from.

steps.title: The proof does not work: a missing sheet is different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. A ספר תורה missing a sheet is an incomplete version of what it is meant to be, while a חומש is a complete scroll of its own book.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that is not so. There, the scroll is lacking within its own matter. Here, it is not lacking within its own matter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the בית מדרש's proof by showing the two cases are not alike.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ספר תורה is supposed to contain all five books, so one missing sheet leaves it broken and incomplete. A חומש is only meant to hold one book, and that book is all there, so it is not 'missing' anything. רבי יוחנן's rule therefore tells us nothing about חומשים.

keyTerms.meaning: but it is not so, a phrase used to reject an argument
lacking within its own matter, meaning incomplete compared to what it is meant to be

steps.confusionAlert: This rejection does not say a חומש is allowed. It only shows that the proof from רבי יוחנן does not work. The actual ruling comes in the next step, for a different reason.

phrases.english: But it is not so:
there, it is lacking within its own matter;
phrases.notes: That scroll is supposed to be a whole Torah, and part of it is missing.

phrases.english: here, it is not lacking within its own matter.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא הִיא, הָתָם מְחַסַּר בְּמִילְּתֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 4.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof. It does not decide the law about חומשים.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The two cases differ: a ספר תורה missing a sheet is incomplete, but a חומש is a complete copy of its one book.

steps.title: No reading from חומשים, out of respect for the community
steps.stepSummary: רבה and רב יוסף rule that one does not read from חומשים in shul, because of כבוד צבור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה and רב יוסף both say: One does not read from single-book scrolls in the synagogue, out of respect for the community.
steps.whatsHappening: Now the actual ruling is given: one may not read from a חומש in shul, but the reason is the community's honor, not that the scroll is incomplete.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The step before showed that a חומש is not 'missing' anything. Even so, using a partial scroll for the public reading is beneath the dignity of the community, so the law is still that it is not allowed. The reason changes, but the result is the same as the בית מדרש wanted.

keyTerms.meaning: the honor or dignity of the community
both of them

steps.whatToRemember: One does not read from a חומש scroll in shul. The reason is כבוד צבור, not that the scroll is incomplete.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the halacha that the public Torah reading must be done from a full ספר תורה.

phrases.english: Rabba and Rav Yosef, who both say:
One does not read from single-book scrolls in the synagogue,
because of the honor of the community.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה וְרַב יוֹסֵף דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ: אֵין קוֹרְאִין בְּחוּמָּשִׁין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof is rejected, gives the ruling with a new reason.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may not read in public from חומשים, because of כבוד צבור.

steps.title: No reading on שבת from a scroll of only הפטרות
steps.stepSummary: רבה and רב יוסף also rule that it is forbidden to read on שבת from a scroll that has only the הפטרות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבה and רב יוסף both say: It is forbidden to read from this scroll of הפטרות on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: A second ruling from the same pair: a scroll with only the הפטרות may not be used on שבת. The next step will ask why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This moves from the Torah reading to the הפטרה from נביאים. The ruling is stated first, and its reason comes right after.

keyTerms.meaning: a scroll containing only the הפטרות
forbidden

phrases.english: And Rabba and Rav Yosef, who both say:
This scroll of הפטרות,
it is forbidden to read from it on Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּה וְרַב יוֹסֵף דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ: הַאי סֵפֶר אַפְטָרָתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, related ruling by the same רבנים as step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may not read on שבת from a scroll of only הפטרות.

steps.title: Asking for the reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why a הפטרות scroll is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the ruling in step 7, which sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since step 6 gave כבוד צבור as its reason, we might guess the same reason applies here. The גמרא asks so it can give the specific reason for this case.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why is it forbidden to read from a scroll of only הפטרות?

steps.title: Because such a scroll should not be written
steps.stepSummary: The reason is that a scroll of only הפטרות should not be written in the first place.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it was not given permission to be written.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: the הפטרות scroll is forbidden because writing such a scroll is not allowed at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason here is not כבוד צבור, as it was for the חומש. The problem is the scroll itself: the words of נביאים are meant to be written as whole books, not copied out in pieces. A scroll that should not exist is not used for the reading.

keyTerms.meaning: it was not given permission to be written

steps.whatToRemember: רבה and רב יוסף forbid reading from a הפטרות scroll because it should not be written. Step 11 rejects this and allows both moving it and reading from it.

phrases.english: Because it was not given permission to be written.
phrases.notes: He means נביאים should be written as complete books, not cut up into separate pieces.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּלֹא נִיתַּן לִיכָּתֵב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A scroll of only הפטרות is not permitted to be written, so it may not be read from.

steps.title: מר בר רב אשי: even moving the scroll is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: מר בר רב אשי adds that a הפטרות scroll may not even be moved on שבת, since it is not fit for reading.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר בר רב אשי said: it is even forbidden to move it. Why? Because it is not fit to read from.
steps.whatsHappening: מר בר רב אשי goes further than רבה and רב יוסף. He says you may not even move a הפטרות scroll on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His logic builds on Step 9. Since such a scroll should never have been written, it is not fit to read from. Something with no permitted use is treated as מוקצה, so it may not be moved on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: To move or carry an object around (on שבת)
What is the reason?
Not fit or usable
To read from it

phrases.english: Mar bar Rav Ashi said:
To move it is also forbidden.
phrases.notes: "It" is the scroll that has only the הפטרות, from Step 7.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
Because it is not fit to read from.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: לְטַלְטוֹלֵי נָמֵי אָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the reason in Step 9 to forbid moving the scroll as well
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A הפטרות scroll may not even be moved on שבת, because it is not fit to read from.

steps.title: The scroll may be moved and read
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects מר בר רב אשי and rules that one may both move a הפטרות scroll and read from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that is not so. It is permitted to move it, and it is permitted to read from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says מר בר רב אשי is wrong. It goes further and allows reading from the scroll too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This rejects more than the ban on moving it. It also overturns the earlier ban on reading from it (Step 7). The proof for this comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: But that is not so: the גמרא's way of rejecting a view
Permitted

steps.confusionAlert: Don't stop at moving it. The גמרא here also allows reading from the scroll, even though Step 7 forbade it.

phrases.english: But that is not so;
it is permitted to move it
and it is permitted to read from it –

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא הִיא, שְׁרֵי לְטַלְטוֹלֵי וּשְׁרֵי לְמִיקְרֵי בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects Step 10 and also overturns the reading ban of Step 7
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the ban on moving the scroll and also the ban on reading from it
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The claim that the scroll is unfit is wrong, because writing it is allowed when there is no other way (proved in the next step).

steps.title: Proof from the book of אגדה and עת לעשות לה׳
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש read from a written book of אגדה on שבת. That writing was allowed under עת לעשות לה׳, and the same applies to a הפטרות scroll.
steps.simpleTranslation: For רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש would read from a book of אגדה on שבת. But such teachings were not supposed to be written down! Rather, since there was no other way, we apply "It is time to act for ה׳; they have nullified Your Torah." Here too, since there is no other way, "It is time to act for ה׳; they have nullified Your Torah."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves Step 11 from what great אמוראים did. They read on שבת from a book that, in principle, should not have been written.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה שבעל פה was not supposed to be written. But because people could not remember it otherwise, writing it was allowed under the rule of עת לעשות לה׳. In the same way, not everyone can afford full books of נביאים. So writing a הפטרות scroll is allowed, which means it may be moved and read from.

keyTerms.meaning: A book of אגדה: non-legal teachings of the Sages
Was not given to be written down
Since there is no other way
"A time to act for ה׳": when needed for Torah's sake, a normal rule may be set aside

steps.whatToRemember: A הפטרות scroll may be moved and read on שבת. Writing it is allowed under עת לעשות לה׳, just like writing down the תורה שבעל פה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is one of the key sources showing that writing down the תורה שבעל פה was allowed only because it was needed.

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ
phrases.english: For Rabbi Yochanan and Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish
would read from a book of aggada on Shabbat;
but it was not given to be written down!
phrases.notes: "It" is the Oral Torah, which was meant to stay spoken, not written.

phrases.english: Rather, since there is no other way,
"It is time to act for the Lord; they have nullified Your Torah";
phrases.notes: תהלים 119:126

phrases.english: here too, since there is no other way,
"It is time to act for the Lord; they have nullified Your Torah."

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ מְעַיְּינִי בְּסִפְרָא דְאַגַּדְתָּא בְּשַׁבְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the proof for the ruling in Step 11
steps.raayaObject: That a הפטרות scroll may be moved and read on שבת
steps.raayaSupportSource: The practice of רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש reading a book of אגדה on שבת, allowed through עת לעשות לה׳

steps.title: אביי asks: may one write a single section for a child?
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רבה whether one may write a scroll with only part of the Torah so a child can learn from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי asked רבה: May one write a scroll with one section of the Torah for a child to learn from?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins. אביי asks whether a partial Torah scroll may be written for teaching a child.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This builds on the idea that some partial scrolls are not normally allowed to be written. The question is whether teaching a child is a good enough reason to permit one.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked him: a real question put to a teacher
Here: a scroll with only one section of the Torah
A young child
To learn from it

phrases.english: Abaye asked Rabba:
What is the law about writing a scroll for a child
phrases.notes: He means a scroll with just one section of the Torah, not the whole תורה.

phrases.english: to learn from?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ אַבָּיֵי מֵרַבָּה: מַהוּ לִכְתּוֹב מְגִילָּה לְתִינוֹק לְהִתְלַמֵּד בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new but related question about writing partial scrolls
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a single Torah section may be written for a child's learning

steps.title: The question applies under both views of how the Torah was given
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that אביי's question can be asked whether the Torah was given section by section or all at once.
steps.simpleTranslation: The question can be asked according to the one who says the Torah was given scroll by scroll. It can also be asked according to the one who says the Torah was given complete.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next move. It says אביי's question works under both opinions, and it will explain each side next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known disagreement about how the Torah was given. One view: משה wrote it section by section over time. The other: he wrote it all at once at the end. One might think the answer simply follows that debate, but the גמרא says the question stays open under both views.

keyTerms.meaning: The question can be asked
According to the one who says
Given scroll by scroll: written in sections over time
Given sealed: written as one complete book at the end

phrases.english: The question can be asked according to the one who says:
the Torah was given scroll by scroll;
and it can be asked according to the one who says:
the Torah was given sealed.
phrases.notes: "Sealed" means finished. משה wrote it all down at once at the end.

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּיבְּעֵי לְמַאן דְּאָמַר: תּוֹרָה מְגִילָּה מְגִילָּה נִיתְּנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Frames the question from Step 13 under both views
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Showing that the question stays open no matter which view of the Torah's giving we follow

steps.title: The two sides under the view that the Torah was given scroll by scroll
steps.stepSummary: Under the scroll-by-scroll view, maybe one may write single sections as it was first given. Or maybe not, since the Torah was later joined into one.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the one who says the Torah was given scroll by scroll: since it was given scroll by scroll, we may write a single scroll. Or perhaps, since it was later joined together, it stays joined.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains both sides of the question under the first view. It does not decide yet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one: the Torah was first given in separate sections, so writing a section alone matches how it began. Side two: once the sections were joined into one Torah, that joining is final. If so, we may no longer write sections separately.

keyTerms.meaning: We may write
Or perhaps: brings in the other side of a question
It was joined or attached together

phrases.english: The question can be asked according to the one who says
the Torah was given scroll by scroll –
since it was given scroll by scroll, we may write a separate scroll;
or perhaps, since it was joined, it stays joined.
phrases.notes: Once the sections became one Torah, maybe we can't split them up again.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דִּמְגִילָּה מְגִילָּה נִיתְּנָה, כּוֹתְבִין; אוֹ דִילְמָא, כֵּיוָן דְּאִידְּבַק אִידְּבַק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first half of the framing in Step 14
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the Torah's original giving in sections permits writing sections now, or its later joining forbids it

steps.title: The question also applies if the Torah was given all at once
steps.stepSummary: Even under the view that the תורה was given complete, we can ask: does that forbid partial scrolls, or does practical need allow them?
steps.simpleTranslation: And let the question be asked also according to the one who says the תורה was given complete. Since it was given complete, maybe one may not write a partial scroll. Or perhaps, since it is not always possible to write a whole one, we do write it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes laying out אביי's question. It shows that the question also exists under the second view, that the תורה was given all at once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the 'all at once' view, the obvious side is to forbid, since the תורה never existed as separate sections. The other side is practical: a child cannot always learn from a full ספר תורה, so maybe we allow it anyway. So the question stands under both views.

keyTerms.meaning: The תורה was given complete, all at once
Let it be asked; the question still applies
Since it is not possible
We write

phrases.english: Let it be asked according to the one who says
the Torah was given complete:
since it was given complete, one may not write a partial scroll;
or perhaps, since it is not possible,
phrases.notes: Not possible to always have a whole ספר תורה for the child to learn from.

phrases.english: we do write it?

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּיבְּעֵי לְמַאן דְּאָמַר תּוֹרָה חֲתוּמָה נִיתְּנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the second half of the setup begun in step 14, after step 15 covered the section-by-section view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether practical need allows writing a partial scroll even if the תורה was given all at once.

steps.title: רבה rules that a partial scroll may not be written
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that one may not write a partial scroll, and the reason is simply that this is the rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: one may not write. And what is the reason? Because one may not write.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers אביי: it is forbidden to write a scroll with only part of the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'reason' sounds circular, but רבה is saying the ban is a fixed rule. Practical need does not override it. This ruling is now the target of אביי's challenges.

keyTerms.meaning: One may not write
And what is the reason?

steps.confusionAlert: Don't get stuck on the answer sounding like it repeats itself. רבה means: there is a set rule against writing partial scrolls, so no extra reason is needed.

phrases.english: He said to him: One may not write it.
And what is the reason? Because one may not write a partial scroll.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֵין כּוֹתְבִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in steps 13 to 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A partial תורה scroll may not be written, even for a child.

steps.title: Challenge from the golden tablet with the סוטה section
steps.stepSummary: אביי objects: הילני המלכה made a golden tablet with פרשת סוטה written on it, which looks like a single section written alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: He objected: She too made a tablet of gold, on which the section of סוטה was written!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רבה's ruling from a משנה about a golden tablet with one תורה section on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a single section, the סוטה section, could be written by itself on a tablet, then partial writing seems allowed. That contradicts רבה's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised an objection against him
A tablet of gold
The section about a woman suspected of unfaithfulness (במדבר 5)

phrases.english: He objected: She too made
phrases.notes: 'She' is הילני המלכה. This line comes from a משנה in יומא listing gifts to the בית המקדש.

phrases.english: a tablet of gold
on which the section of סוטה was written!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ: אַף הִיא עָשְׂתָה טַבְלָא שֶׁל זָהָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבה's ruling in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's ruling that one may not write a partial scroll.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A single תורה section was written on its own on the tablet, so partial writing must be allowed.

steps.title: The tablet had only first letters
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש, quoting רבי ינאי, answers that the tablet was written in אלף בית: only the first letters of the words.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן לקיש said in the name of רבי ינאי: It was written in אלף בית.
steps.whatsHappening: The challenge is answered. The tablet did not hold the real text, only first letters to help the writer remember.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If only first letters were written, the tablet is not a real written section of the תורה. So it does not count as a partial scroll, and רבה's rule stands.

keyTerms.meaning: In letters only, the first letter of each word
In the name of

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יַנַּאי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said in the name of Rabbi Yannai:
It was written in alef-beit.
phrases.notes: Just the first letter of each word, as a memory aid, not the full words.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יַנַּאי: בְּאָלֶף בֵּית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case: the tablet was not full text.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The tablet held the complete סוטה section.
steps.terutzMaskana: The tablet held only first letters, so it is not a written section of the תורה.

steps.title: Challenge: the writer copies what is written on the tablet
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the כהן copies 'what is written on the tablet', which suggests the full text was there.
steps.simpleTranslation: He objected: When he writes, he looks and writes what is written on the tablet!
steps.whatsHappening: A new challenge attacks the 'first letters only' answer, using a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the כהן copies exactly 'what is written' on the tablet, the tablet must have held the full words. Otherwise he could not copy it. That would undo the answer of step 19.

keyTerms.meaning: Looks and writes; he copies
What is written

phrases.english: He objected: When he writes,
phrases.notes: He is the כהן writing the scroll for the סוטה.

phrases.english: he looks and writes what is written on the tablet!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ: כְּשֶׁהוּא כּוֹתֵב, רוֹאֶה וְכוֹתֵב מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּטַּבְלָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the tablet held only first letters.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Copying 'what is written' means the tablet held the same full text he writes.

steps.title: Read it as 'like what is written'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adjusts the wording to 'like what is written on the tablet', meaning the tablet only guided him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say: 'like what is written on the tablet'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by changing one word of the ברייתא, so it no longer proves the tablet had full text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Like what is written' means the tablet reminds him of what to write. He does not copy it letter for letter. So first letters alone are enough, and the answer of step 19 survives.

keyTerms.meaning: Say; read the text this way
Like what is written

phrases.english: Say: "like what is written on the tablet."
phrases.notes: Only one word changes. 'Like' means the tablet guides him; he isn't copying it exactly.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא: כְּמָה שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּטַּבְלָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changes the wording of the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He copies exactly what is on the tablet.
steps.terutzMaskana: He writes according to the tablet, using it as a memory guide.

steps.title: Challenge: the tablet contained full words
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא says what was on the tablet: 'אם שכב' and 'אם לא שכב'. Those are full words of the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: He objected: When he writes, he looks at the tablet and writes what is written on the tablet. What is written on the tablet? 'If he lay', 'if he did not lay'!
steps.whatsHappening: A stronger challenge comes from a ברייתא that quotes full words from the tablet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the wording cannot just be adjusted. The ברייתא names actual full words that appeared on the tablet. That seems to prove the tablet was not only first letters.

keyTerms.meaning: If he lay (with you); words from the סוטה section
If he did not lay (with you)

phrases.english: He objected: When he writes,
he looks at the tablet and writes
what is written on the tablet.
What is written on the tablet?
"If he lay," "if he did not lay"!
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:19-20

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ: כְּשֶׁהוּא כּוֹתֵב, רוֹאֶה בַּטַּבְלָא וְכוֹתֵב מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּטַּבְלָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Renews the attack on step 19's answer after step 21's fix, with a source that names full words.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the tablet held only first letters.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says full words of the פסוק were written on the tablet.

steps.title: The tablet alternated full words and first letters
steps.stepSummary: The tablet was written בסירוגין: some full words and some first letters, so it still was not a full written section.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are we dealing with here? It was written in alternation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the tablet had a mix: some full words, like 'אם שכב', and the rest in first letters only.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fits both sources. Full words appeared, but the section was never fully written out. So the tablet still is not a partial ספר תורה. The proof against רבה falls away, and his ruling that one may not write a partial scroll stands.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here?
In alternation; mixing full words and first letters

steps.whatToRemember: רבה rules that one may not write a scroll with only part of the תורה. The golden tablet of הילני המלכה is no proof against this. It held only first letters, or a mix of full words and first letters, never the full section.

phrases.english: What are we dealing with here?
It was written in alternation.
phrases.notes: Some words were written in full, and the rest were written only as first letters.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן – בְּסֵירוּגִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 22 and protects רבה's ruling of step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case: a mixed writing style.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since full words appeared, the tablet held the full section.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only some words were full; the rest were first letters, so it is not a written section of the תורה.

steps.title: The question is already a dispute among תנאים
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that writing a partial scroll for a child is a dispute between the תנא קמא and רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like a dispute of תנאים: One may not write a scroll with only part of the Torah for a child to learn from. But if the writer plans to finish the whole Torah later, it is permitted. רבי יהודה says: In ספר בראשית, one may write up to the generation of the flood. In תורת כהנים (ספר ויקרא), one may write up to 'And it was on the eighth day.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show that the question of writing a small scroll for a child is already argued about by תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא forbids a partial scroll unless the writer plans to finish the whole Torah. רבי יהודה allows a partial scroll, but only up to certain set points: the flood in בראשית, and the eighth day in ויקרא. So the question becomes a disagreement between two תנאים, not just an open question.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Like the תנאים': this question is already a dispute among תנאים
A scroll with only part of the Torah
A young child
He plans to complete it (the whole Torah)
Another name for ספר ויקרא

phrases.english: It is like a dispute of Tannaim:
One may not write a scroll for a child
to learn from it,
but if his intention is to complete it, it is permitted.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
In Bereishis, until the generation of the flood.
In Toras Kohanim, until "And it was on the eighth day."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 9:1. תורת כהנים is ספר ויקרא.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּתַנָּאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion of the סוטה tablet and shows that the larger question of writing a partial scroll is a dispute among תנאים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תנא קמא forbids a partial scroll for a child unless the writer plans to finish it; רבי יהודה allows it up to set points in בראשית and ויקרא.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the Torah was given scroll by scroll
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, quoting רבי בנאה, says the Torah was given section by section, based on a פסוק in תהלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי בנאה: The Torah was given scroll by scroll, as it says: 'Then I said, here I have come with the scroll of a book written about me.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the first side of a new dispute: רבי יוחנן says the Torah was given in separate sections over time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks of 'the scroll of a book', which sounds like one section being its own scroll. From this, רבי יוחנן learns that each part of the Torah was given as a separate scroll when it was said, and only later joined together.

keyTerms.meaning: It was given scroll by scroll, one section at a time
The earlier sage whom רבי יוחנן quotes here
The scroll of a book

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי בְּנָאָה:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Bana'a:
The Torah was given scroll by scroll,
as it says:
"Then I said, here I have come
with the scroll of a book written about me."
phrases.notes: תהלים 40:8.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי בְּנָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the dispute about how the Torah was given, first mentioned in step 14, and gives its source and author.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The Torah was given section by section, each as its own scroll.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: the Torah was given as one complete book
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says the Torah was given complete, all at once, based on a פסוק in דברים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן לקיש says: The Torah was given complete, as it says: 'Take this book of the Torah.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the other side of the dispute: ריש לקיש says the Torah was given as one finished book.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק tells them to 'take this book of the Torah', which sounds like one whole book. So ריש לקיש holds the Torah was written down as a single completed book, not in separate pieces.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'sealed'; here it means complete and finished
Take
The book of the Torah

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish says:
The Torah was given sealed,
phrases.notes: 'Sealed' here means finished: written down as one whole book.

phrases.english: as it says: "Take this book of the Torah."
phrases.notes: דברים 31:26.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite view to רבי יוחנן, with its own פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The Torah was given as one complete book.

steps.title: How does רבי יוחנן explain 'Take this book'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי יוחנן deals with ריש לקיש's פסוק, which speaks of one whole book.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one (רבי יוחנן), isn't it written 'Take'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן: the פסוק 'Take this book of the Torah' seems to show the Torah was one whole book.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the Torah was given in separate scrolls, why does the פסוק talk about taking one whole 'book of the Torah'? רבי יוחנן must explain this פסוק in a way that fits his view.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one too: what does the other side do with this פסוק?
Isn't it written?

phrases.english: And the other one too,
phrases.notes: Here 'the other one' is רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: isn't it written "Take"!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ נָמֵי, הָכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns ריש לקיש's פסוק against רבי יוחנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's view that the Torah was given scroll by scroll
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Take this book of the Torah' speaks of one complete book, which seems to go against giving it in separate pieces.

steps.title: That was after the scrolls were joined
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers for רבי יוחנן that 'Take this book' was said after the separate scrolls had been joined into one.
steps.simpleTranslation: That פסוק is about after it was joined together.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי יוחנן: by the time משה said 'Take this book', the separate parts had already been put together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sections were given one at a time over the years in the desert. At the end, they were joined into one book, and that is when the פסוק says 'Take this book.' So the פסוק fits רבי יוחנן's view.

keyTerms.meaning: After
That it was joined (stuck together)

phrases.english: That is after it was joined together.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא לְבָתַר דְּאִידְּבַק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against רבי יוחנן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Timing: the פסוק describes a later stage
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Take this book' shows the Torah was always one whole book.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק refers to the end, after the separate scrolls were joined into one book.

steps.title: How does ריש לקיש explain 'the scroll of a book'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how ריש לקיש deals with רבי יוחנן's פסוק, which speaks of a scroll.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one (ריש לקיש), isn't it written 'with the scroll of a book written about me'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now challenges ריש לקיש: the פסוק in תהלים talks about a 'scroll', which seems to show the Torah came in separate pieces.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the Torah was given as one complete book, why does the פסוק call it a 'scroll of a book'? ריש לקיש needs to explain this פסוק too.

keyTerms.meaning: Written about me

phrases.english: And the other one too,
phrases.notes: Now 'the other one' is ריש לקיש.

phrases.english: isn't it written "with the scroll of a book written about me"!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ נָמֵי, הָכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors the previous challenge, now turning רבי יוחנן's פסוק against ריש לקיש.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's view that the Torah was given complete
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'scroll' in תהלים seems to show the Torah came in separate scrolls.

steps.title: The whole Torah can be called a scroll
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers for ריש לקיש that the whole Torah is called a 'scroll', as seen from a פסוק in זכריה.
steps.simpleTranslation: That פסוק teaches that the entire Torah is called a scroll, as it is written: 'And he said to me, what do you see? And I said, I see a flying scroll.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for ריש לקיש: the word 'scroll' does not mean a small piece. Even the whole Torah is called a 'scroll'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא answers for ריש לקיש with a proof from זכריה, where the whole Torah is called a 'flying scroll'. So 'scroll of a book' in תהלים can mean the complete Torah, and it does not prove it was given in pieces. Both sides can now explain both פסוקים, so the dispute stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: Is called
A flying scroll (from זכריה)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן: the Torah was given scroll by scroll and joined at the end. ריש לקיש: it was given as one complete book, and the word 'scroll' can mean the whole Torah.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think ריש לקיש rejects the word 'scroll'. He agrees the Torah is called a scroll; he just says the word can mean the whole Torah, not only a single section.

phrases.english: That one teaches that the entire Torah
is called a scroll,
as it is written: "And he said to me, what do you see?
And I said, I see a flying scroll."
phrases.notes: זכריה 5:2.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַהוּא, דְּכׇל הַתּוֹרָה כּוּלָּהּ אִיקְּרִי מְגִילָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against ריש לקיש; step 31 then offers a second answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefinition of a word, supported by another פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Scroll' means one separate section, so the Torah came in pieces.
steps.terutzMaskana: The whole Torah is called a 'scroll' (זכריה), so the פסוק fits a Torah given complete.

steps.title: A second way for ריש לקיש to explain the 'scroll' פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers ריש לקיש another answer: the 'scroll' פסוק hints to the sections listed in רבי לוי's teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you prefer, the 'scroll' פסוק is there to hint to what רבי לוי taught.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives ריש לקיש a second, different answer for the 'scroll' פסוק. It is setting up the next step, where רבי לוי's teaching is quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first answer said the whole Torah can be called a 'scroll'. This new answer says the 'scroll' refers to one specific group of sections, the ones in רבי לוי's teaching. Either way, the פסוק no longer proves that the whole Torah was given scroll by scroll.

keyTerms.meaning: Alternatively; or, another way to answer
For the teaching of רבי לוי; the פסוק is needed to hint to it

steps.confusionAlert: This is still ריש לקיש's answer about the 'scroll' פסוק. It is not a new opinion that argues with ריש לקיש.

phrases.english: Alternatively, [it comes] for that of Rabbi Levi
phrases.notes: This is ריש לקיש's second way to read the 'scroll' פסוק (תהלים 40:8): it hints to the sections רבי לוי is about to list.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי נָמֵי, לְכִדְרַבִּי לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to the challenge of step 29, alongside the answer given in step 30.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the פסוק: it refers to a specific set of sections, not the whole Torah.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 'scroll' פסוק seemed to prove רבי יוחנן's view that the Torah was given scroll by scroll.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק can be read as pointing only to the sections in רבי לוי's teaching, so ריש לקיש's view still stands.

steps.title: רבי לוי: eight sections were said on the day the משכן was set up
steps.stepSummary: רבי לוי teaches that eight Torah sections were said on the day the משכן was set up, and the גמרא begins listing them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי לוי said: Eight sections were said on the day the משכן was set up. They are: the section of the כהנים, the section of the לוים, the section of the impure, the section about sending the impure away, and the section of 'אחרי מות'...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי לוי's teaching that eight sections were all said on one day, the day the משכן was set up. It starts listing them, and the list continues afterward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These eight sections were said together on a single day, so they form their own group. This explains why the פסוק could call them a 'scroll'. So far five of the eight are named.

keyTerms.meaning: Sections of the Torah
The משכן was set up
People who are ritually impure
Sending impure people out of the camp
'After the death', the opening words of a Torah section

phrases.english: As Rabbi Levi said:
Eight sections were said
on the day that the Tabernacle was set up,
these are they:
the section of the priests, and the section of the Levites,
and the section of the impure, and the section of sending away the impure,
and the section of 'After the death',
phrases.notes: ויקרא 16.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי לֵוִי: שְׁמֹנֶה פָּרָשִׁיּוֹת נֶאֶמְרוּ בַּיּוֹם שֶׁהוּקַם בּוֹ הַמִּשְׁכָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the teaching of רבי לוי that step 31 pointed to.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eight Torah sections were said on the day the משכן was set up: the כהנים, the לוים, the impure, sending away the impure, 'אחרי מות', and more still to be listed.
